description: Gregorian leap-year test with % 4, % 100 and % 400 not folded to the branchless (y & (y % 25 ? 3 : 15)) == 0
notes: Found while screening C candidates. Textbook leap-year test written by us. clang trunk -O3 -march=skylake keeps a branch and two urem (by 100 and 400): 11 IR instructions. expected.ll is the branchless full-range form given in Falk Hüffner's post (is_leap_year3; once y is a multiple of 4, divisibility by 100 and 400 reduces to 25 and 16): 6 IR instructions. The three-instruction multiply-and-mask test of the same post is only valid for y <= 102499, so it is not used. No LLVM issue found for this pattern. Gain estimated by llvm-mca (godbolt llc and llvm-mca trunk, -mcpu=skylake, cycles per 100 iterations): 460 vs 236. expected.ll proven correct (refinement) by Alive2 alive-tv, 2026-10-28: src = clang trunk -O3 IR of src.c (godbolt cclang_trunk, -O3 --target=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -march=skylake -emit-llvm -S -g0) renamed @src, tgt = expected.ll renamed @tgt, identical signature; output 'Transformation seems to be correct!' with no warning. Run on Alive2's own Compiler Explorer instance (alive2.llvm.org/ce, compiler id 'alive'), since godbolt.org does not host alive-tv.
